parts.text: Drinking water isn’t just H₂O – though there are over 15 septillion molecules of it in a standard glass. It also contains natural

, dissolved organic and biological matter, and substances that enter from agriculture, industry, consumer products and water treatment.

Most of these substances are harmless at the concentrations typically found in water. Some are beneficial, and even

, such as sodium, fluoride and calcium ions, which build strong bones and teeth. Additionally, these ions balance electrolytes that regulate bodily function.

In fact, drinking large quantities of completely demineralized or distilled water can

the body’s electrolyte balance. This water would dilute the natural sodium levels in blood, potentially causing hyponatremia, a condition with symptoms such as nausea, headache, confusion and seizures.

Most people encounter water-quality science through an

report from their local water company. It’s usually a couple of pages long with chemical names and numbers in a table. It lists various compounds that may exist in the water, summarizes what has been found in tests of the water source, and explains whether the water meets government-set standards that

and protect public health and safety.

These reports provide important information about drinking water safety, but they are not a complete inventory of every substance scientists can

or are working to understand.

We
study a range of contaminants, chemical and biological, that are found in drinking water, with the goal of developing technologies to further safeguard public health. This includes pollutants and

that are not included on an annual water report.

A secret world of sneaky water pollutants

Consider perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, more commonly known as PFAS and also called “forever chemicals” because they

in the environment for a long time. These are a large family of chemicals used in consumer products because they resist water, oil and heat.

Research has linked exposure to certain PFAS with adverse chronic health effects, such as endocrine disruption, low birth weight in

and certain types of cancer.

Federal drinking water standards now limit the amount of two common types of PFAS found in the environment to 4 parts per trillion, a level extremely hard to detect even on advanced analytical equipment. However, the broader chemical family includes many others whose
and health effects are less understood by scientists and completely missed by the public or policy.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Dry climates can increase river nitrate pollution even far from intensive human activity.
The sinking of a large ship creates an artificial reef that marine organisms will gradually colonise.
Routine water-quality reports cover only part of what matters for understanding drinking water.
Periods without wind or sunshine create challenges for electricity systems that depend on renewables.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: It lists various compounds that may exist in the water, summarizes what has been found in tests of the water source, and explains whether the water meets government-set standards that promote and protect public health and safety.

questions.prompt: Why are some substances in drinking water beneficial?
options: They guarantee that all contaminants are harmless.
They eliminate the need for minerals in the body.
They prove that water never needs testing.
They contribute to functions such as building bones and teeth.
questions.explanation: 第 3 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Some are beneficial, and even essential, such as sodium, fluoride and calcium ions, which build strong bones and teeth.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 9?
options: It lists various compounds that may exist in the water, summarizes what has been found in tests of the water source, and explains whether the water meets government-set standards that promote and protect public health and safety.
study a range of contaminants, chemical and biological, that are found in drinking water, with the goal of developing technologies to further safeguard public health.
Research has linked exposure to certain PFAS with adverse chronic health effects, such as endocrine disruption, low birth weight in fetuses and certain types of cancer.
Consider perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, more commonly known as PFAS and also called “forever chemicals” because they persist in the environment for a long time.
questions.explanation: 定位第 9 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Consider perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, more commonly known as PFAS and also called “forever chemicals” because they persist in the environment for a long time.
